subject: Tenant boundary & network isolation — follow-up and action plan
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay.mehta@healthbridge.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 May 2028 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Tenant boundary & network isolation — post-demo recap

Hi Sanjay / Alyssa (cc'd if helpful),

Thanks again for the call today — really useful to see the HealthBridge ingestion pipeline and the compliance bar you need for PHI-parity workloads. Below is a short recap plus a proposed next step list so we can align on whether Dedicated or Private VPC makes the most sense for you.

Quick recap from our side:
- Primary requirement: strict data isolation for patient-identifiable datasets; network egress must be controllable via customer-managed firewall rules.
- Secondary: key material management (BYOK/KMS integration) and control-plane residency in a customer VPC for auditability.
- Ops constraint: minimal changes to your existing VPC peering policy; you prefer an approach that avoids long lead-time networking projects.

Open questions we flagged during the demo:
1) Do you need physical tenant isolation (dedicated hosts) or is logical isolation (single-tenant VPC + strong network controls) sufficient?
2) Is HealthBridge able to host a customer-managed VPC subnet where we can place the inference nodes, or would you prefer Redwood to run dedicated hardware in our Dedicated pool with tightened egress controls?
3) What compliance documents / attestation do you need in addition to our SOC 2 excerpt? (I attached the SOC snippet we referenced.)

Proposed next steps (short):
- Sanjay / Alyssa: confirm whether you require physical hardware isolation (dedicated hosts) vs just separate customer VPC with strict egress.
- If physical isolation required: we'll have Ben run an initial fit assessment and surface estimated capacity/cost and lead-time.
- If VPC-residency suffices: Connor will draft a network runbook and a checklist for peering/VPN setup.

Attachments: network-segmentation-diagram.png (sample), SOC2-excerpt.pdf (redacted excerpt).

Thanks — I’ll leave the priority call to you, Sanjay. If you want, we can schedule a short ops call next week to walk the diagram.

Best,
Hannah
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay.mehta@healthbridge.io>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alyssa King <alyssa.king@healthbridge.io>
Date: Fri, 31 May 2028 10:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Tenant boundary & network isolation — post-demo recap

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the clear notes — confirmed with our security team this morning. Short answers:
- For regulated PHI workloads we have a current preference for physical isolation (dedicated hosts) because our auditors call this out in current control language; however, logical isolation with customer-managed VPC + strong attestations could be acceptable if you can provide: (a) proof of no co-tenant data plane connectivity, (b) KMS BYOK guarantee, and (c) control-plane/service-account audit logs retained for 12 months.
- HealthBridge can host a customer-managed VPC subnet in AWS us-east-1 but we prefer to avoid complex BGP peering; a private VPC with AWS Transit Gateway attachment or a short-lived VPN is our preferred pattern.
- Documents needed: SOC2 excerpt (thank you), an architecture diagram that explicitly highlights host tenancy model, and a statement of KMS integration pattern.

We remain on a tight timeline — ideally a procurement decision by the end of Q3. Next step: can Ben or someone from your engineering side produce a short technical note that maps Dedicated vs Private VPC to the three auditor asks above? That would let our compliance team do a pass.

Best,
Sanjay
Dir, Security & Platform Engineering
HealthBridge.io

Date: Fri, 31 May 2028 18:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Tenant boundary & network isolation — post-demo recap

Hannah / team,

I can take the tech note. Proposed outline I’ll circulate tomorrow:
1) Quick definitions: what we mean by "physical tenant isolation" (dedicated hosts vs dedicated GPU pool) vs "VPC residency" (customer VPC with Redwood-managed agents).
2) Evidence mapping to their auditor asks: network adjacency proof (flow logs/host tenancy), KMS/BYOK integration (architectural flow + supported KMS vendors), control-plane residency & audit logs (what we expose in Private).
3) Operational differences: provisioning lead-time, capacity scaling, patching/maintenance responsibilities, expected monthly cost delta.

I’ll include a short runbook for Transit Gateway/VPN options and a sample security FAQ for procurement. Connor — can you pull a template network runbook we used for Medisys? That will speed things up.

-Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay.mehta@healthbridge.io>, Alyssa King <alyssa.king@healthbridge.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 01 Jun 2028 14:22:00 +0000
Subject: Redwood action plan & MAP — Dedicated vs Private VPC fit for PHI workloads

Hi Sanjay / Alyssa,

Per Ben's note, we put together a compact mutual action plan (MAP) and a short evidence pack we'll deliver next week. High-level MAP:
- By 2028-06-04: Ben to deliver a 2-page technical note mapping Dedicated vs Private VPC to your auditor asks (network tenancy, KMS, audit logs). Attachment: draft skeleton (network-segmentation-diagram.png).
- By 2028-06-07: Connor to provide a one-page network runbook for Transit Gateway + short-lived VPN option (includes sample cloudwatch flow-logs config).
- By 2028-06-12: Redwood to provide a KMS BYOK integration note and a redactable control-plane audit log sample (redwood will provide log schema only; full logs by NDA).
- Decision checkpoint: joint call w/ your security and procurement week of 2028-06-19 to review and align on either Dedicated or Private VPC for the PoC.

Sizing/cost indicator: if you choose Dedicated (physical tenant isolation) expect a 25–40% upcharge vs a functionally equivalent Private VPC deployment at small scale, mostly driven by dedicated hardware reservation and maintenance windows. We’ll include a ballpark capacity estimate in Ben’s note.

Please confirm if MAP timeline looks workable. If you prefer an earlier procurement review, we can compress the durations but will need early access to one of your compliance contacts for quick clarifying Qs.

Thanks — happy to set the ops call.

Best,
Hannah

Attachments referenced: network-segmentation-diagram.png, SOC2-excerpt.pdf

From: Alyssa King <alyssa.king@healthbridge.io>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay.mehta@healthbridge.io>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Jun 2028 09:47:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Redwood action plan & MAP — Dedicated vs Private VPC fit for PHI workloads

Hannah / Ben — thanks, this is helpful and the timeline is reasonable. Two quick clarifications from procurement/security: 
- Our auditors accept the audit-log schema if we can demonstrate 12 months of immutable retention; if Redwood can provide a log-archive pattern (S3 with MFA delete or equivalent) that's ideal.
- For the KMS BYOK note: we use AWS KMS (multi-tenant keys today) but can move key material to a dedicated CMK under our account if needed — we'll need to see the exact handshake sequence (rotate/remove access when contract ends).

We’ll aim to get a compliance SME on the June 19 call. Thanks again, and we look forward to Ben’s note.

—Alyssa
Head of Procurement, HealthBridge.io
